subject: Metered-burst credit mechanics, passback timing and distributor holdback for Azure private offer
messages:
From: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@clearwave.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Azure private offer questions — metered burst credits and distributor holdback

Hi Diego,

Thanks for taking the time on our call this morning. Quick follow-up from procurement as we prepare an internal recommendation: we need the private offer to spell out how metered \"burst\" credits are delivered and reconciled, the invoice cadence (monthly true-up vs quarterly), and how distributor holdbacks are handled so we can model cashflow.

Specifically: 
- We expect a monthly invoice but want a 30-day true-up window for metered overage credits. Can Redwood issue an invoice that shows the gross charge, the metered burst credit, and the net?
- Our channel agreement requires a 10% distributor holdback on list price that can be released after a 90-day usage verification. Can Redwood accommodate a holdback that sits on our side and is passed back on final reconciliation, or does Redwood prefer escrow/withhold on invoice?
- We need an example of how reseller pass-through will work if we set an 8% reseller fee in the PO.

Attaching our draft SOW for context. We aim to finalize commercial terms this week so we can lock the private offer.

Thanks,
Marta Gomez
Sr. Procurement Manager
ClearWave Corp
Attachment: ClearWave_SOW_draft.pdf
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@clearwave.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwave.com
Date: 2025-06-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer questions — metered burst credits and distributor holdback

Hi Marta — appreciate the clear list. Summary answers below and a proposed invoice/PO template attached. Short version: yes, we can produce the monthly invoice with line-level burst credits and support a distributor-side holdback workflow; we generally avoid holding customer funds on our ledger for extended escrow but will support passback on reconciliation.

Proposed commercial mechanics (high level):
- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing, Net 30. Metered usage and burst credits appear on the invoice as separate line items: gross consumption, burst credit, net due.
- Burst credits: delivered as a recurring monthly credit bucket sized to the commit tier and consumed intra-month. Any overage beyond the committed burst is billed and reconciled on the next invoice.
- True-up: monthly true-up with 30-day dispute window (customer-led). Final annual true-up can be requested if needed by procurement.
- Distributor holdback: Redwood prefers passback on reconciliation (customer retains holdback), with Redwood applying the passback amount on settlement after usage verification. If ClearWave requires Redwood-side escrow, we can discuss but it will require legal/finance signoff and slightly different invoicing language.
- Reseller pass-through: we can set an 8% reseller fee as a separate line on the PO; Redwood will not reduce that fee on our end and will honor the pass-through allocation in monthly settlements.

Recommended channel split (proposal): 8% reseller pass-through, 4% distributor holdback (released on monthly reconciliation once usage confirms), with an optional 2% marketing co-op included as a separate rebate line if needed. Ben and Soojin are copied to confirm channel economics.

I attached a PO template showing line-level entries and sample calculations. If that structure looks ok, we can draft the private offer and send to DocuSign.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: RW-Azure-PO-template.xlsx
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-18T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: ClearWave — confirm channel margin and holdback appetite

Team — forwarding ClearWave's procurement ask (below) and my proposed mechanics. Need quick read: is a 4% distributor holdback defensible vs their requested 10%? Legal also needs to confirm whether passing back on customer reconciliation (our preferred flow) is contractually ok.

Questions:
- Ben: can you run the margin calc for 8% reseller / 4% holdback vs 8% / 10%? What's the impact at the list price levels in the template?
- Soojin: any ops limitations on us supporting a monthly line-level credit for burst and net-billing?
- Laura: if we need Redwood-side escrow language, what are the legal requirements and SLA impact?

Cc'ing ClearWave is fine if we resolve quickly; want to keep momentum this week.

Thanks, Diego
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-18T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: ClearWave — confirm channel margin and holdback appetite

Diego — ran two quick scenarios and attached the calc. Short take:
- 8% reseller + 4% passback is workable and keeps net economics within acceptable thresholds for starter commit tiers.
- If ClearWave insists on 10% holdback, we either need to raise list price ~3.5-4% or reduce Redwood net by ~2-3% to preserve unit economics. That will be a sticking point for small commits.
- Ops note: recommend we treat the holdback as customer-retained funds and do passback on the monthly reconciliation rather than Redwood escrow. That avoids additional billing complexity and reduces bookkeeping for finance.

I attached the channel margin workbook with scenario toggles. Laura: if we need escrow, we'll need legal to draft a holdback release annex (one-time effort).

Ben
Attachment: channel_margin_calc.xlsx
From: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@clearwave.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwave.com
Date: 2025-06-19T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer questions — metered burst credits and distributor holdback

Diego — thanks, that reads clean. We discussed internally and prefer the passback-on-reconciliation approach (customer holdback released on monthly true-up) rather than Redwood escrow. ClearWave can accept a 4% distributor holdback and 8% reseller pass-through for the initial 12-month commit tier, with an annual true-up.

Next steps: please send the DocuSign PO (using your template) with the line-level burst credit language and monthly reconciliation clause. Procurement wants the DocuSign by EOD Wednesday so we can route to finance.

On the DocuSign, please include: 1) sample invoice layout; 2) the channel split table; 3) the true-up timing clause.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Marta
Sr. Procurement Manager
ClearWave Corp
